stem:
Kunal buys a bag with marked price $\mathrm{Rs}\,1000$. The shop gives a $20\%$ discount, then a further $10\%$ discount on the reduced price.

Which claim correctly finds the final price?

options.text: Final price $= \mathrm{Rs}\,1000 \times 0.7 = \mathrm{Rs}\,700$, adding the $20\%$ and $10\%$ labels.
Final price $= \mathrm{Rs}\,1000 \times 0.8 \times 0.9 = \mathrm{Rs}\,720$, applying $20\%$ then $10\%$ on the new base.
The same successive-base calculation is required when the shop gives only a single $20\%$ discount.
Final price $= \mathrm{Rs}\,1000$ because $20$ and $10$ are the printed percent labels.

teacher.key_rationale: Successive discounts use the changed amount as the next base: 1000×0.8×0.9=720. Adding percent labels, applying successive logic to a single discount, or reading the printed percents as the price miss the hinge.
